dmc.t003: Damage Cancel (DMC) is a phenomenon where, when multiple players attack the same monster at the same time, one player’s damage overwrites another player’s damage, causing it to effectively disappear.
dmc.t005: In PSO, damage is handled in a very specific way.
dmc.t006: When a player attacks a monster, the client sends data to the server based on the monster's max HP minus its current HP, not the actual damage dealt.
dmc.t007: regardless of the actual damage dealt.
dmc.t008: This includes 0 damage hits and status effects such as Jellen and Zalure.
dmc.t009: The server then forwards this information to the other players.
dmc.t012: The attack only applies status effects such as Jellen or Zalure
dmc.t014: The server forwards this damage data to all other players.
dmc.t015: However, the server has a critical flaw:
dmc.t016: it always applies the most recently received damage data, no matter what.
dmc.t017: It does not compare values or check which damage was higher or lower.
dmc.t019: If two or more players attack a monster at nearly the same time,
dmc.t020: one player’s damage can overwrite another player’s damage.
dmc.t021: Because of this, the monster may appear to take far less damage than expected,
dmc.t022: even while being heavily attacked by multiple players.
dmc.t024: DMC is most noticeable when using rapid-fire weapons that deal repeated 0 damage, for example weapons like Last Swan.
dmc.t025: If 0-damage packets are constantly sent, they can repeatedly overwrite real damage,
dmc.t026: making other players' attacks effectively useless and the monster appear almost invincible.
dmc.t028: Attacks that miss due to ATA do not send damage data
dmc.t029: However, when a special attack fails to activate, a damage packet is sentand can still trigger DMC
dmc.t031: Damage Cancel (DMC) is a PSO server-side issue where simultaneous attacks can overwrite each other,
dmc.t032: especially due to frequent or 0-damage hits, causing monsters to take far less damage than expected.
